claims.text: An FCC Ti-containing high-entropy alloy can achieve room-temperature Hc above 100 Oe by introducing a nanoscale secondary phase into the FCC matrix.
The nanoscale secondary phase may be Ti-rich BCC or ordered L12.
A single-phase FCC solid solution has low anisotropy and coercivity because its orbital moments are suppressed.
A Fe-Co-Ni-Cr-Ti alloy can serve as a single-phase FCC starting matrix.
Adding 5-15 at.% Ti to a Fe-Co-Ni-Cr base and aging it can induce nanoscale secondary-phase precipitation while retaining an FCC matrix.
VEC can predict whether an HEA solid solution favors FCC or BCC structure.
Maintaining VEC above 8.0 will ensure that the Fe-Co-Ni-Cr-Ti matrix remains FCC.
Aging between 600 and 900 degrees Celsius for 1-10 hours will produce the proposed precipitate structure.
The resulting precipitates will be embedded within, rather than replace, the FCC matrix.
The secondary-phase precipitates act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Ti promotes formation of a phase having a different crystal structure or magnetic anisotropy from the FCC matrix.
The A2 nanoparticles observed in Al28Co20Cr11Fe15Ni26 provide an analogue for the proposed secondary phase.
The secondary phase creates local magnetic anisotropy and domain-wall pinning that increase coercivity.
Interfacial anisotropy in the dual-phase structure overcomes the low coercivity of the single-phase FCC state.
Ti addition helps preserve a high Curie temperature by avoiding Mn-induced paramagnetism or magnetic frustration.
The designed alloy will have Tc above 350 K.
The designed alloy will have room-temperature Hc above 100 Oe.
The resulting microstructure will contain 5-15 vol.% secondary phase with precipitate diameters below 50 nm.
Single-phase FCC Fe-Co-Ni-Cr-Ti alloys typically have Hc below 20 Oe.
A paramagnetic or antiferromagnetic secondary phase may fail to increase coercivity, whereas a ferromagnetic or high-anisotropy phase is required.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and boundary require formation of a suitable secondary phase, but the falsification rule says that obtaining a single-phase FCC alloy with low Hc at 20 at.% Ti would falsify that requirement. Such a result merely shows that this composition and treatment failed to create the required mediator and is consistent with the stated hypothesis.

The predicted threshold is Hc above 100 Oe, but the dual-phase falsification threshold is Hc below 50 Oe. A reproducible dual-phase result between 50 and 100 Oe would violate the prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
